title: CLI: Add llm friendly docs to the ai prepare command
body:
Closes #

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

## What I did

This PR essentially adds a new section to the ai prepare command, which teaches it how to follow documentation when needed:
```
│  ### Storybook Documentation Reference
│  When you need to look up Storybook APIs, concepts, or examples, use these
│  LLM-optimized URLs:
│  - Full docs index: https://storybook.js.org/llms.txt
│  - Code snippets only: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-stories.md?renderer=react&language=ts&codeOnly=true 
│  Key documentation pages for this task:
│  - Writing stories: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-stories.md?renderer=react&language=ts
│  - Decorators: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-stories/decorators.md?renderer=react&language=ts
│  - Args: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-stories/args.md?renderer=react&language=ts
│  - Play functions: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-stories/play-function.md?renderer=react&language=ts
│  - Vitest integration: https://storybook.js.org/docs/10/writing-tests/vitest-plugin.md?renderer=react&language=ts 
│  Fetch these URLs directly when you need guidance on Storybook APIs or patterns.
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Fix React+Vite gate condition (currently allows unsupported combinations).**

Lines 63-64 use `&&`, so the check only fails when *both* renderer and builder are wrong. For a strict “React with Vite only” gate, this must be `||`.

<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  if (
-    projectInfo.rendererPackage !== '@storybook/react' &&
-    projectInfo.builderPackage !== '@storybook/builder-vite'
-  ) {
+  if (
+    projectInfo.rendererPackage !== '@storybook/react' ||
+    projectInfo.builderPackage !== '@storybook/builder-vite'
+  ) {
```
</details>

```suggestion

    projectInfo.builderPackage !== '@storybook/builder-vite'
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>


_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Incorrect fallback produces invalid import statement.**

When `rendererPackage` is `null`, the fallback `'react'` generates an invalid import `from 'react'` instead of `from '@storybook/react'`. According to the `ProjectInfo` interface, `rendererPackage` contains the full package name (e.g., `"@storybook/react"`), so the fallback should match that format.



<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    ${projectInfo.hasCsfFactoryPreview ? getCsfFactoryExample() : getCsfExample(projectInfo.rendererPackage || 'react')}
+    ${projectInfo.hasCsfFactoryPreview ? getCsfFactoryExample() : getCsfExample(projectInfo.rendererPackage || '@storybook/react')}
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    ${projectInfo.hasCsfFactoryPreview ? getCsfFactoryExample() : getCsfExample(projectInfo.rendererPackage || '@storybook/react')}
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/lib/cli-storybook/src/ai/prompt.ts` at line 96, The call that builds the
CSF example uses a wrong fallback string for rendererPackage; update the
expression that passes rendererPackage into getCsfExample so it falls back to
the full package name "@storybook/react" instead of "react" (i.e., change the
argument to use projectInfo.rendererPackage || '@storybook/react'); this will
ensure getCsfExample and any imports it generates use the expected full package
format—check uses of projectInfo and the getCsfExample invocation to apply the
fix.
```

</details>
